title: Extending THAPI with CXI Hardware Counter Sampling for High Resolution NIC Telemetry
problem: Existing HPC tracing tools lack insight into low-level network interface controller (NIC) behavior; NIC hardware counters revealing congestion and retries remain underutilized despite providing critical performance information
motivation: HPC applications are sensitive to network variability. Modern NICs like HPE Slingshot-11 Cassini provide detailed hardware counters, but integration with standard tracing frameworks is lacking, limiting diagnostic capabilities.
method: The work adds a sampling plugin to THAPI, a framework that records detailed traces of what high-performance computers are doing. This plugin periodically reads hardware counters from CXI network cards (Cassini Interconnect) — essentially built-in meters that measure network congestion, retries, and other low-level network metrics. The iprof tool weaves these periodic measurements into the main trace timeline, and Perfetto visualizes everything together so you can see when network problems happen and what the application was doing at that moment.
key_novelty: This work is the first to combine measurements from network hardware (NIC hardware counters tracking congestion and retries) with an HPC tracing system, showing network problems and application behavior in a single timeline.
contributions: CXI hardware counter sampling plugin design for THAPI framework
Negligible overhead at typical sampling rates
Exposure of previously hidden performance factors: congestion delays, load imbalances
New diagnostic capabilities demonstrated on point-to-point and collective communication patterns
limitations: Abstract lacks specific overhead numbers and congestion detection statistics; limited to Cassini NIC (vendor-specific); generalization to other NICs unclear
